nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. The adjoint of the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, is the weighted backward shift $B_w$, given by $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$; that is, $S_w^* = B_w$.
nodes.title: Adjoint of the weighted shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$, and on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ let $S_w$ be the weighted forward shift, $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, and $B_w$ the weighted backward shift, $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$. Then $(B_w S_w x)_i = |w_i|^2 x_i$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and…
nodes.title: The weighted backward shift after the forward shift is diagonal

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with $|w_n| = 1$ for every $n$. On $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ let $S_w$ be the weighted forward shift, $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, and $B_w$ the weighted backward shift, $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$. Then $B_w S_w$ is the identity operator.
nodes.title: The weighted backward shift is a left inverse for unimodular weights

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $w, v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be bounded sequences, that is, there are constants $C$ and $D$ with $|w_n| \le C$ and $|v_n| \le D$ for all $n$. Then $w - v$ is bounded: there is a constant $E$ with $|w_n - v_n| \le E$ for all $n$.
nodes.title: Differences of bounded sequences are bounded

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be bounded, that is, $|w_n| \le C$ for all $n$ for some constant $C$, and let $N \in \mathbb{N}$. Then the truncation $w^{(N)}$ of $w$ after $N$ coordinates, given by $w^{(N)}_n = w_n$ for $n < N$ and $w^{(N)}_n = 0$ for $n \ge N$, is bounded as well.
nodes.title: Truncated weights are bounded

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with $w_n \neq 0$ for every $n$. Then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, is injective.
nodes.title: Weighted shifts with nonzero weights are injective

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence of weights, that is, $|w_n| \le C$ for all $n$ for some constant $C$. The weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, which sends $x$ to $(0, w_0 x_0, w_1 x_1, \dots)$, is a compact operator if and only if $w_n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Compactness criterion for weighted shifts

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence of weights, and suppose there is $N \in \mathbb{N}$ with $w_n = 0$ for all $n \ge N$. Then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, which sends $x$ to $(0, w_0 x_0, w_1 x_1, \dots)$, is a compact operator.
nodes.title: Weighted shifts with eventually vanishing weights are compact

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. The weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, is an isometry if and only if $|w_n| = 1$ for every $n$.
nodes.title: Isometric weighted shifts

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the sequence $(\overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1})_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ is square-summable.
nodes.title: Weighted backward shifts preserve square-summability

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the sequence $y$ with $y_0 = 0$ and $y_{n+1} = w_n x_n$ is square-summable.
nodes.title: Weighted forward shifts preserve square-summability

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. The weighted backward shift $B_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$, has operator norm $\|B_w\| = \sup_n |w_n|$.
nodes.title: Norm of the weighted backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$, and let $B_w$ be the weighted backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$. Then $\|B_w x\| \le (\sup_n |w_n|)\, \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: Norm bound for the weighted backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with $|w_n| = 1$ for every $n$. Then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, satisfies $\|S_w x\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: Weighted shifts with unimodular weights preserve norms

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and let $S_w$ be the weighted forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. If $C$ is a real number with $|w_n| \le C$ for every $n$, then the operator norm of $S_w$ is at most $C$.
nodes.title: Uniform weight bounds bound the weighted shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. The weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ has operator norm $\|S_w\| = \sup_n |w_n|$.
nodes.title: Operator norm of a weighted shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the weighted forward shift $S_w$, viewed as a linear map, satisfies $\|S_w x\| \le \left(\sup_n |w_n|\right) \|x\|$.
nodes.title: Norm bound for weighted shift images

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. If $w_n = 0$ for some $n$, then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is not injective.
nodes.title: A vanishing weight makes the weighted shift non-injective

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and let $S_w$ and $B_w$ be the weighted forward and backward shifts on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the composite $S_w B_w$ satisfies $(S_w B_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w B_w x)_i = |w_{i-1}|^2 x_i$ for every $i \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Forward-after-backward weighted shift is diagonal

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence with $w_n \to 0$. For $N \in \mathbb{N}$ let $w^{(N)}$ be the truncation of $w$ after $N$ coordinates, with $w^{(N)}_n = w_n$ for $n < N$ and $w^{(N)}_n = 0$ for $n \ge N$, and for bounded weights $u$ let $S_u$ be the weighted forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, sending $x$ to…
nodes.title: Weighted shifts with truncated weights converge in operator norm

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, and let $N, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge N$. Then the truncation $w^{(N)}$ of $w$ after $N$ coordinates (equal to $w_k$ for $k < N$ and to $0$ for $k \ge N$) satisfies $w^{(N)}_n = 0$.
nodes.title: Truncated weights vanish from the cutoff on

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, and let $N, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n < N$. Then the truncation $w^{(N)}$ of $w$ after $N$ coordinates (equal to $w_k$ for $k < N$ and to $0$ for $k \ge N$) satisfies $w^{(N)}_n = w_n$.
nodes.title: Truncated weights agree with the weights below the cutoff

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For a sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the truncation of $w$ after $N$ coordinates is the sequence $w^{(N)}$ with $w^{(N)}_n = w_n$ for $n < N$ and $w^{(N)}_n = 0$ for $n \ge N$.
nodes.title: Truncated weights

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and let $B_w$ be the weighted backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of $B_w x$ is the weighted backward-shift function of $w$ applied to $x$ at $i$, that is,…
nodes.title: Coordinates of the weighted backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. With every weight equal to $1$, the weighted backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the canonical backward shift.
nodes.title: Unit weights give the plain backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and write $e_n$ for the $n$-th standard basis vector of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $n$, the weighted backward shift $B_w$ satisfies $B_w e_{n+1} = \overline{w_n}\, e_n$.
nodes.title: Weighted backward shift on basis vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. The weighted backward shift $B_w$ is the bounded operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ obtained by applying the backward shift $(x_0, x_1, \dots) \mapsto (x_1, x_2, \dots)$ and then multiplying coordinate $i$ by $\overline{w_i}$; thus $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Weighted backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For weights $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the weighted backward-shift function of $w$ applied to $x$ takes the value $\overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$ at $i$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the weighted backward-shift function

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For weights $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, the weighted backward shift of $x$ is the sequence whose term at index $i$ is $\overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Weighted backward shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the image of $x$ under the weighted backward shift with weights $w$, regarded as a linear map on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, is as a sequence the weighted backward shift of $x$: its term at index $i$ is $\overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$…
nodes.title: The weighted backward shift linear map agrees with the shift of sequences

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$. The weighted backward shift linear map with weights $w$ is the bounded weighted backward shift operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ with weights $w$, regarded as a $\mathbb{K}$-linear map from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ to itself (forgetting continuity).
nodes.title: Weighted backward shift as a linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the image of $x$ under the weighted forward shift operator with weights $w$ is as a sequence the weighted forward shift of $x$: its term at index $0$ is $0$ and its term at index $n + 1$ is $w_n x_n$ for every $n$.
nodes.title: The weighted forward shift agrees with the shift of sequences

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$, and let $S_w$ be the weighted forward shift operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ with weights $w$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate $(S_w x)_i$ is the term at index $i$ of the weighted forward shift of the sequence $x$;…
nodes.title: Coordinates of the weighted forward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The weighted forward shift operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ whose weights are all equal to $1$ is the unilateral forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The weighted forward shift with unit weights is the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$, and let $(e_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be the standard basis vectors of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $n$, the weighted forward shift operator with weights $w$ sends $e_n$ to $w_n e_{n+1}$.
nodes.title: The weighted forward shift on basis vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $w, v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be sequences such that $w$, $v$ and $w - v$ are bounded. Writing $S_u$ for the weighted forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ with bounded weights $u$, sending $x$ to $(0, u_0 x_0, u_1 x_1, \dots)$, we have $S_{w - v} = S_w - S_v$.
nodes.title: Weighted shift of a difference of weights

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$. The weighted forward shift with weights $w$ is the bounded operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ obtained by first applying the diagonal operator $x \mapsto (w_n x_n)_{n}$ and then the unilateral forward shift $(x_0, x_1, \dots) \mapsto (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$.
nodes.title: Weighted forward shift operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For weights $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the term at index $n + 1$ of the weighted forward shift of $x$ is $w_n x_n$.
nodes.title: Weighted forward shift at a successor index

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For all weights $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and every sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, the term at index $0$ of the weighted forward shift of $x$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Weighted forward shift at index zero

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For a weight sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, the weighted forward shift of $x$ is the sequence $y$ with $y_0 = 0$ and $y_{n+1} = w_n x_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Weighted forward shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be a weight sequence whose norms $\|w_n\|$ are bounded above. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the image of $x$ under the weighted forward shift linear map, viewed as a sequence, is the weighted forward shift of $x$: its coordinate $0$ is $0$ and its coordinate $n + 1$ is $w_n x_n$ for every $n$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the weighted forward shift linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be a weight sequence whose norms $\|w_n\|$ are bounded above. The weighted forward shift linear map is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ underlying the bounded weighted forward shift operator (multiplication by $w$ followed by the forward shift), which sends $x$ to…
nodes.title: Weighted forward shift as a linear map
Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
